newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish farmers may grow gene-modified maize.
newsitem.headline: Spanish farmers may grow gene-modified maize.

text.p: Spanish farmers may start growing gene-modified maize next year now that the European Union has approved it for import from the United States, Spain's maize growers' association AGPM said on Thursday.

"Now it has been approved, we will certainly consider growing it as it has many advantages and we need to remain competitive in the face of U.S. imports," said Augustin Marine, chairman of the maize growers' association AGPM.
But another national farmers group complained that there was as yet insufficient proof that the grain was safe.
"There is a lack of sufficient historic and scientific perspective to know the real effects of this genetically-altered grain," the farmers' group COAG said in a statement.
"We are therefore informing farmers of the potential dangers for the environment and human and animal health," it added.
The EU Commission decided on Wednesday to clear for production the controversial gene-altered maize developed by Swiss firm Ciba-Geigy AG and grown in the U.S.
AGPM's Marine said Spanish farmers would be eager to plant the maize if it really proved to be more competitive than existing unaltered grain.
"Clearly we need to study the advantages for Spanish farmers more closely but if it proves more attractive farmers could start planting it in April in time for the next harvest," he said.
The maize, altered to make it resistant to the corn-borer crop pest and increase its tolerance of certain weedkillers, has already been approved by U.S. authorities.
A spokesman for French maize producers said on Wednesday French farmers would also start sowing the modified maize as early as next spring if the seed prices were right.

Environmental groups have condemned the EU decision which removes any restrictions on selling the modified maize on EU markets as a food or seed. They say the manipulated maize could reduce the efficiency of certain antibiotics.
